facts.text: The library does carry release paths: `Connection` has a destructor and the verbs table includes `dealloc_pd`, `destroy_qp` and `destroy_cq`. The reported leak is therefore not a missing call in JACCL's own code path as read here; it matches the reports that the kernel side does not return PDs after teardown.

A larger mesh or more wires per pair burns the pool faster per init, so a 5-node mesh should hit the limit in fewer restarts than a 2-node pair. The reported counts do not fit this simple model (about 60 sessions at 2 nodes against 2 to 3 broadcasts at 5 nodes), so other consumers of the pool probably exist (orphans, probes).
Ring init allocates a PD, a completion queue and a queue pair per connection, `2 * n_conns` PDs per rank
Mesh init allocates a PD per connection to every peer, so a rank uses `(size - 1) * n_wires` PDs
JACCL registers each send and receive buffer to the PD of the connection it serves
JACCL's verbs table includes `dealloc_pd`, `destroy_qp` and `destroy_cq` and `Connection` has a destructor
mlx-lm issue 955 recommends one N-node broadcast over N-1 sequential 2-node transfers to limit init cycles, and periodic reboots for heavy use
mlx-lm issue 955 says RDMA device names change after every reboot, so `mlx.distributed_config --auto-setup` must be rerun and the hostfile redistributed after a PD-exhaustion reboot
